phases.objective: Implement an unmounted async SQL authority store for Tenant-exclusive allowlists and Workspace Owner approvals while retaining migration and mount boundaries.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Hostinger Storage Durable Tenant Authority Store Guard
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Allowlists and approvals support exact registration replay, bounded CAS updates, immutable token-history enforcement, readback, rollback, and export without route mount, provider dispatch, or migration apply.
steps: Require signed schema verification bound to the exact three-table authority-store contract and exact deployed runtime parity.
Create the canonical store without opening a database connection or exposing the raw pool.
Register a Tenant-exclusive allowlist and persist its initial revision token in immutable history.
Replay the exact allowlist while rejecting an ID collision with different evidence.
Advance allowlist revisions through row-version CAS and reject a previously used revision token with rollback.
Register and replay a Workspace Owner approval, then advance its evidence token through CAS.
Reject reused approval evidence, shared/platform scope, unsafe fields, and non-Workspace-Owner approval authority.
Export a secret-free durable snapshot while runtime, route, worker, provider, migration, and production flags remain false.
assertions: Current authority rows and immutable token history are written in one transaction under the shared advisory lock.
Every insert and update requires exact same-transaction readback.
Allowlist revisions and approval evidence digests can never be reused after replacement.
The contract-local DDL is not placed in the runtime migration directory or promoted into Wave 1 through Wave 3.
The current synchronous memory-only Tenant Canary is not modified and compatibility remains false.
No route, server, worker, provider, Hostinger, deployment, main, or Production mutation occurs.

phases.objective: Promote and apply the schema through a separately authorized migration cycle, capture signed live readback, and connect the store through the async Tenant runtime bridge.
blockers: The contract-local DDL has not been promoted into a checksum-bound runtime migration sequence.
No live migration authorization, dry-run, apply, or same-cycle table/index/constraint readback exists.
No signed live authority-store schema verification exists.
The current Tenant Canary remains synchronous and memory-factory-owned.
No route or worker mount authorization exists.

phases.objective: Prove restart reconstruction, concurrent CAS conflicts, interrupted token-history writes, stale readback cycles, and durable revocation behavior.
This slice does not execute a live Tenant or database canary.
Production schema apply, runtime mount, and provider dispatch remain separately governed and blocked.
